beats.lead: AI's first collapse had an author
beats.note: In 1972 Britain's Science Research Council asked an outsider to survey artificial intelligence. He was a fluid dynamicist, not a computer scientist.

beats.name: James Lighthill
beats.role: His survey concluded that in no part of the field had the discoveries produced 'the major impact that was then promised.' British funding collapsed; the work survived at just Edinburgh, Essex and Sussex.

beats.text: The general purpose robot is a mirage.
beats.note: The BBC staged the debate under that title in its Controversy series: Lighthill versus McCarthy, Michie and Gregory at the Royal Institution, May 1973. The recording still circulates.

beats.lead: The name arrived a decade late
beats.note: Coined at a 1984 AAAI debate, where Schank and Minsky warned the new boom would collapse the same way. Three years later the billion-dollar AI industry did.

beats.text: The second winter arrived on schedule.

beats.line: Britain paid £350 million to restart what one report stopped.
